title: CLIP: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training
reading: The slide introduces CLIP, summarising it in two bullets. In training, an image encoder and a text encoder are jointly learned to predict which (image, text) pairs actually belong together within a batch. At test time, the resulting model supports zero-shot, open-vocabulary classification of an image. The slide credits Radford et al., 'Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision', ICML 2021.

concepts.name: CLIP
concepts.why_it_matters: Contrastive image-text pretraining that underpins much of modern multimodal and zero-shot vision.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning over batch pairings
concepts.why_it_matters: The training objective: correct (image, text) pairs are matched against in-batch negatives.

concepts.name: Zero-shot, open-vocabulary classification
concepts.why_it_matters: Enables classifying into arbitrary label sets described in text, without task-specific training.

concepts.name: Image/text encoders
concepts.why_it_matters: CLIP assumes familiarity with separate modality encoders producing embeddings.
